guards.what: N1: `CardPileCmd.Add(card, PileType.Deck)` (Storybook.cs:20) vs `run.add_card` (run.py:341-354) -- the INSERTION POSITION and the two deck hooks
guards.rationale: Checked against PROMPT.md bug class 8 (append position), which relic/arcane_scroll left as an open question. CardPileCmd.Add reaches CardPile.AddInternal with the default `index = -1`, whose else-arm is `_cards.Add(card)` -- an APPEND at the end of the deck (CardPile.cs:83-97). run.add_card appends too (run.py:349). It also dispatches the same two hooks in the same order: Hook.ModifyCardBeingAddedToDeck before the append (run.py:345-348) and the AfterCardChangedPiles-for-deck analogue after it (run.py:352-353), matching CardPileCmd's deck arm at CardPileCmd.cs:379-396. EXECUTED (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b15.py b15-misc): after add_relic('storybook') the deck tail is ['brightest_flame']. Rule 7: run.py, CardPileCmd.cs and CardPile.cs are not hashed here.

guards.what: N2: `Hook.ShouldAddToDeck` is consulted by CardPileCmd's deck arm (CardPileCmd.cs:384) and the sim has no such hook
guards.rationale: VOCABULARY RULING (2026-07-26 relic fix pass), applied at every dead-in-the-source site in this tier so it stops contradicting itself. When a C# member the sim omits is DEAD IN THE GAME SOURCE ITSELF -- zero overrides, zero producers, zero callers anywhere under src/ -- the correct verdict is `faithful`, not `waiver`. PROMPT.md v6 item 3, which the relic stream itself wrote, settles the principle for the mirror-image case: 'a waiver is in-scope-adjacent and declined, and here there is no source behaviour to be faithful to.' A waiver claims something in scope was deliberately not audited; here there is nothing to decline, because the member provably cannot fire in any run of the shipping game and cannot become live by porting more content -- it would take a change to the game's own source. `faithful` also states the stronger and more useful fact: the two codebases have the SAME observable. Before this pass the relic tier split 8 waivers against 5 faithfuls on identical reasoning; these entries are now all `faithful` (binding rule 3). NOTE: this ruling does NOT touch MULTIPLAYER gates (`player != base.Owner`, `Players.Count == 1`), which stay `waiver` -- the shared contract names multiplayer as out of scope outright, and unlike a dead member a player count really can differ in the shipping game; the sim simply does not model that mode. AT THIS SITE: Cited and matched from relic/calling_bell guard G4 (binding rule 3, one verdict per mechanism), which reached the finding by execution: `grep -rn should_add_to_deck sts2_rl/ --include=*.py` returns ZERO hits, and `grep -rn ShouldAddToDeck src/` returns only the dispatch (CardPileCmd.cs:384), the Hook wrapper (Hook.cs:2084-2088) and the base declaration (AbstractModel.cs:2144) -- zero overrides -- so the hook is dead code in C# too. ONLY THE VERDICT CHANGES. Rule 7: CardPileCmd.cs, Hook.cs and AbstractModel.cs are not hashed here.

guards.what: N3: `base.Owner.RunState.CreateCard<BrightestFlame>(base.Owner)` (Storybook.cs:19) vs make_card('brightest_flame') -- is the ported card the right one?
guards.rationale: BrightestFlame.cs:23-25 is `base(0, CardType.Skill, CardRarity.Ancient, TargetType.Self)` with CanonicalVars MaxHpVar(1), EnergyVar(2), CardsVar(2) and one upgrade level (OnUpgrade bumps Energy and Cards by 1). EXECUTED: make_card('brightest_flame') is CardType.SKILL, energy_cost 0, max_upgrade_level 1, eternal False -- so the cost, type and upgrade ceiling all match, and the card joins the deck at upgrade level 0 as CreateCard does. The card's own OnPlay fidelity is the CARD stream's unit, not this record's, and cards/brightest_flame is not hashed here (rule 7).

guards.what: N4: no undo_after_obtained, and no HasUponPickupEffect declaration
guards.rationale: PROMPT.md v6 item 3 (rule-3 resolution): the ABSENCE of undo_after_obtained is faithful at every site -- the helper has no C# counterpart (nothing in the game un-picks a relic), so a sim lacking it is not diverging from the source, which is the only question this audit asks. The deck edit is not run state 'outside run.relics' of the max-HP kind, but it IS unrecoverable on a conformance relic swap, so the same operational caveat as relic/small_capsule N2 applies (a discarded Storybook leaves a Brightest Flame in the deck, which conformance/runner.py:618's (id, upgrade_level) deck comparison would report). Separately: Storybook.cs declares no HasUponPickupEffect override, so the port's default False (relics/base.py:96) is correct -- and it is moot for IsTradable because Ancient rarity already excludes it (relics/base.py:132-136).
